ruling: ADR_UGENCE_AUTHORITY_PLANE_SCOPING.md AP-3 IDP_VALIDATED_FIRST (controlling, section 18); protocol and status in section 20
status_note: Designated 2026-09-11 by the owner: Cloudflare Access (team 'ugence') backed by Google Workspace (ugence.ai) is the enterprise issuer; the non-production Access application 'AP3 Enterprise Issuer Validation' on ap3-validation.ugence.ai admits the Google group ugence-ap3-test@ugence.ai, test principal ap3-test@ugence.ai. AP-3 is NOT met: no row of the validation matrix has been executed against the real issuer (every 'result' below is null), and the conformance_harness block records why each row is still blocked. The worker's in-process issuer is implementation and conformance evidence only and never satisfies this gate. Every field below is configuration, never a secret: client secrets, private keys, cookies and test tokens stay in the identity provider, Cloudflare, the CI secret store or approved runtime custody.

designation.ap3_enterprise_issuer: Cloudflare Access, team 'ugence', backed by Google Workspace (Workspace domain ugence.ai); non-production Access application 'AP3 Enterprise Issuer Validation' protecting ap3-validation.ugence.ai; policy 'Google Workspace group' (Allow) admitting ugence-ap3-test@ugence.ai; test principal ap3-test@ugence.ai. accounts.google.com is the login method behind Access, not the application JWT issuer
designation.jwks_trust: configured JWKS endpoint https://ugence.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/certs (IA-3: no OIDC discovery; default TLS verification; keys cached by kid, refreshed once on an unknown kid, then fail closed)
designation.tenant_claim: UNRULED: the owner's mapping is 'ugence.ai, accepted only when issuer and audience validate and the verified email belongs to the exact ugence.ai domain'. The ratified adapter (IA-4) reads one top-level claim as presented and derives nothing; a Cloudflare Access user token carries no tenant claim [I]. Requires an owner ruling (a Cloudflare-injected claim, or an IA-4 amendment admitting a derived tenant for this issuer) before any tenant row can execute
designation.principal_claim: sub (the Access user's stable issuer-scoped identifier); email is the IdP-verified human-readable address and a directory-binding attribute, never the key
designation.actor_type_claim_or_mapping: UNRULED: the owner's mapping is human = non-empty sub plus verified email; service = common_name present with empty sub; ambiguous = deny. The ratified adapter (IA-4) marks HUMAN only on an exact match of one configured claim against one configured value and never infers HUMAN from sub; type=app is not that claim. Requires an owner ruling (a Cloudflare-injected marker claim, or an IA-4 amendment for this issuer) before the human-actor rows can execute
designation.directory_binding: the Authority Directory principal_id is the issuer-qualified subject reference percent-encoded(iss)|percent-encoded(sub) (ID-2); the verified email is recorded as the display and binding attribute; the Cloudflare Access Google-group policy is admission evidence, never a substitute for an internal role grant (AX-5)
designation.jwks_rotation_behaviour: Cloudflare publishes the current and next signing keys at the certs endpoint and rotates them on its own schedule [I]; the adapter refreshes the JWKS exactly once on an unknown kid and retries verification once, then refuses KEY_UNKNOWN; a JWKS that cannot be fetched is IdentityUnavailable, never an unauthenticated answer; an unsigned payload is never decoded

evidence.identity_provider_classification: Google Workspace Base (ugence.ai) as enterprise identity source; Cloudflare Access (team 'ugence') as application gateway and JWT issuer; Ugence Authority Directory as authorization, role and tenant binding
evidence.test_tenant_classification: non-production; one test principal ap3-test@ugence.ai in Google group ugence-ap3-test@ugence.ai; no production data; the Google Workspace identity-provider test in Cloudflare succeeded and returned the principal with that group membership (owner-reported, 2026-09-11)
evidence.claim_mapping_decisions: iss exact = https://ugence.cloudflareaccess.com; aud must contain the designated application audience; sub required non-empty (adapter REQUIRED_CLAIMS); exp and iat required, nbf honoured when present, all judged against the injected clock; alg RS256 within the IA-2 allowlist; kid required, unknown kid refused after one refresh. OPEN, needing an owner ruling before execution: (1) IA-1 requires header typ at+jwt and a Cloudflare Access token is expected to carry typ JWT [I]; (2) the tenant mapping (see designation.tenant_claim); (3) the actor-type mapping (see designation.actor_type_claim_or_mapping); (4) the proof header: the plane reads X-Ugence-Approver-Proof (AW-3, WRITE_PROOF_HEADER), while Cloudflare injects Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion at the origin; (5) matrix rows 14 to 16 need the AX-5 WriterAuthorizer, which section 19.5 sequences after AP-3
evidence.validation_environment_limitations: the validation slice's execution environment (2026-09-11) has no egress to ugence.cloudflareaccess.com (CONNECT refused by its proxy), so the live JWKS was not fetched and no kid is recorded; no live Access token was obtained and none will ever be stored; the conformance harness below ran against the worker's in-process issuer configured with the designated issuer string and audience, over a loopback JWKS, and is implementation evidence only

must_never_contain: a self-signed or in-process issuer recorded as the enterprise issuer
